ai.title: MODERN METHODS OF SALES FORECASTING: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND BSC (BALANCED SCORECARD)
ai.authors: Dmitriy K. Avritsevich, Nadezda P. Tishkina
ai.venue: BULLETIN OF CHECHEN STATE PEDAGOGICAL UNIVERSITY Series 1 Humane and Social Sciences
ai.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach to enhancing the sales forecasting process, based on the synergy of modern artificial intelligence methods (including machine learning and deep learning technologies) and the Balanced Scorecard (BSC). It justifies the relevance of transitioning from traditional mathematical methods to innovative data analysis algorithms, which enable the processing of large volumes of information and the detection of complex interrelationships that are inaccessible through classical tools. The author’s methodology is based on a combination of end-to-end analytics, dynamic conversion coefficients, and consideration of average check value, and also implies the phased integration of the BSC to ensure the strategic alignment of the company's goals with the operational tasks of the sales department. The paper describes the key criteria for selecting machine learning algorithms (decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, and neural networks) and provides recommendations for the practical application and analysis of big data to improve forecast accuracy. Special attention is given to the development of an intelligent analytical system that supports the principles of the BSC: financial, customer, internal, and learning and growth aspects of the enterprise's activities. The prospects of scaling this system to the entire organization are demonstrated,…

ai.title: Deep learning for time series forecasting: a survey
ai.authors: Xiangjie Kong, Zhenghao Chen, Weiyao Liu et al.
ai.venue: International Journal of Machine Learning and Cybernetics
ai.abstract: Time series forecasting (TSF) has long been a crucial task in both industry and daily life. Most classical statistical models may have certain limitations when applied to practical scenarios in fields such as energy, healthcare, traffic, meteorology, and economics, especially when high accuracy is required. With the continuous development of deep learning, numerous new models have emerged in the field of time series forecasting in recent years. However, existing surveys have not provided a unified summary of the wide range of model architectures in this field, nor have they given detailed summaries of works in feature extraction and datasets. To address this gap, in this review, we comprehensively study the previous works and summarize the general paradigms of Deep Time Series Forecasting (DTSF) in terms of model architectures. Besides, we take an innovative approach by focusing on the composition of time series and systematically explain important feature extraction methods. Additionally, we provide an overall compilation of datasets from various domains in existing works. Finally, we systematically emphasize the significant challenges faced and future research directions in this field.

ai.title: Role of artificial intelligence and learning techniques in time series forecast of PM2.5 data: An extensive review
ai.authors: Ferdin Joe John Joseph, Sannasi Ganapathy
ai.abstract: Nowadays, this survey is necessary to equip the society with enriched Particulate Matter 2.5 (PM2.5) forecasting and enabling the health interventions with decision making policy. For researchers and academicians, this review provides an opportunity to explore the state-of-art about the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques in the process of predicting the future air quality by analyzing the time series air quality data. For this purpose, the various prediction systems have been developed by various researchers in the past for predicting the various life-threatening diseases, natural calamity and air pollution by using statistical approach, ML and Deep Learning (DL) techniques. This article discusses about the various time series forecasting techniques that are developed by using Statistical approach, ML and DL Techniques. Especially, the time series forecasting methods on PM2.5 data are considered in this review by highlighting the method differences and the result comparative analysis. The PM2.5 data is widely used dataset to predict the future air pollution level in the specific regions of the world. In this review, the number of research papers published in these areas. This review shows the various experimental results of the different research works are summarized with respect to the evaluation metrics including Mean Absolute Error and…

ai.title: Utilization Of Artificial Intelligence In Demand Forecasting: A Qualitative Study Of Business Actors
ai.authors: Prendi Purba, Elfan Michael Siahaan, Charles Widianto Hulu et al.
ai.abstract: Market uncertainty in the era of volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity (VUCA) demands that businesses possess high predictive acumen. This study explores the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in demand forecasting through a descriptive qualitative approach. The study focuses on a deeper understanding of how the integration of AI technology transforms managerial decision-making processes and the dynamics of its adaptation within the digital business ecosystem in Indonesia. In-depth interviews were conducted with ten informants holding managerial and operational analyst positions in the e-commerce and technology retail sectors in Indonesia. The results show that the application of AI, particularly based on Machine Learning and Deep Learning, is able to reduce subjective human bias and capture non-linear data patterns that conventional statistical methods fail to identify. This implementation significantly improves inventory estimation accuracy, minimizes holding costs, and prevents loss of sales momentum (stockouts). However, the transition to an AI-based forecasting system faces significant structural challenges, including data quality issues (data silos), limited local talent with multidisciplinary competencies, and cultural resistance within the organization. From the perspective of managerial decision-making theory, AI acts as a cognitive amplification tool,…

ai.title: Sales Prediction Using LSTM and BiLSTM Models: A Deep Learning Approach for Time Series Forecasting
ai.authors: P.A. Arifa, Kishorkumar Devasenapathy
ai.venue: Journal of Wireless Mobile Networks Ubiquitous Computing and Dependable Applications
ai.abstract: Accurate sales forecasting significantly impacts planning strategies, inventory control, and business operations. Traditional methods of forecasting are often inadequate in recognizing intricate, multidimensional trends over time in sales data. This paper focuses on evaluating the performance of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) networks in forecasting sales time series. Due to their sophisticated nature, LSTM and BiLSTM networks are an appropriate choice for sales forecasting since they recognize sequential data patterns and long-range dependencies as well as bidirectional dependencies. This research entails the complete process of sales data from preprocessing and feature engineering to model training using LSTM and BiLSTM networks. Important evaluation metrics such as MAE, RMSE, and MAPE are used to compare the models' performances. Experimental results suggest that BiLSTM significantly outperforms LSTM in recognizing sales fluctuation patterns. This, in turn, generates more accurate forecasts. The results demonstrate the ability of deep learning techniques to improve the precision of sales forecasting and, in turn, assist companies in optimizing resource allocation and increasing profitability. Including factors such as economic indicators, industry benchmarks, and advertising would provide even more value in future model refinement.

ai.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN COMMERCE: APPLICATIONS IN DEMAND FORECASTING AND INVENTORY MANAGEMENT
ai.authors: M. Afrabegam, A. Abinaya, M. Bavadharani et al.
ai.venue: Scholar Journal of Commerce and Management
ai.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an important component of digital transformation in commerce, particularly in activities that depend on the timely interpretation of large and changing datasets. Among these, demand forecasting and inventory management directly influence purchasing, warehousing, distribution and customer service. This paper examines how AI-supported forecasting can connect historical sales, customer behaviour, prices, promotions, seasonal effects and selected external factors with inventory decisions. Using a narrative review of concepts and applications supported by selected peer-reviewed literature on AI and supply chain management, it discusses machine learning, deep learning, time-series analysis and predictive analytics as tools for identifying demand patterns and supporting replenishment decisions. The review indicates that AI can strengthen planning by processing multiple variables at speed, identifying relationships that are difficult to detect manually and supporting more responsive inventory decisions, but it does not remove the need for managerial judgement. Forecast quality depends on the quality and relevance of data, and implementation can be constrained by cost, cybersecurity requirements, skills gaps, system integration and unexpected changes in customer behaviour. The paper therefore presents AI-enabled demand forecasting as a…

ai.title: A Review on the Implementation of Artificial Intelligence for Real-Time Product Pricing and Demand Forecasting Optimization
ai.authors: Mr. Dhananjay Nayak, Ms. Archana Thorat, Hanmant N. Renushe
ai.venue: International Journal Of Recent Advances in Engineering & Technology
ai.abstract: In the contemporary, fast-paced global market environment, organizations need to respond swiftly and effectively to changing consumer expectations, rival pricing schemes, and fluctuating economic conditions. A paradigm shift from traditional, heuristic-based approaches to data-driven, adaptive, and scalable solutions is represented by the incorporation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into pricing and demand forecasting processes. Artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, including machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and reinforcement learning (RL), have shown remarkably effective at identifying latent demand patterns, capturing non-linear relationships, and facilitating real-time dynamic pricing decisions. With a focus on their algorithmic underpinnings, implementation designs, real-world applications, and quantifiable effects on business performance, this paper summarizes the most recent state-of-the-art AI techniques used in product pricing and demand forecasting optimization.The paper also describes potential research routes and discusses current issues such data heterogeneity, model interpretability, and computational complexity. Clarifying the strategic role of AI in promoting revenue optimization, raising customer happiness, and boosting overall operational efficiency across a range of industrial areas is the key goal.

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence in Supply Chain Management: Enhancing Demand Forecasting, Inventory Optimization, and Operational Efficiency
ai.authors: Yasir Khalid, Salman Javed, Muhammad Junaid Hassan et al.
ai.venue: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
ai.abstract: The study explored the impact of AI in Supply Chain Management, specifically on demand forecasting, inventory optimization, and operational efficiency. The data was collected using a structured questionnaire, where a quantitative cross-sectional survey design was used, with 300 professionals from the supply chain, procurement, logistics, inventory, warehousing and operations departments. The questionnaire had a 5-point Likert scale ranging from strongly disagree to strongly agree and measured the usage of Artificial Intelligence, demand forecasting, inventory optimization, and operational efficiency. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistical analysis, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation and linear regression analysis. The results showed high levels of AI utilization (M = 4.18, SD = 0.61), demand forecasting (M = 4.21, SD = 0.59), inventory optimization (M = 4.11, SD = 0.64), and operational efficiency (M = 4.23, SD = 0.58). Demand forecasting (β = .681, p < .001), Inventory optimization (β = .647, p < .001), and Operational efficiency (β = .710, p < .001) had high positive relationships with AI. The regression models accounted for 46.4%, 41.9% and 50.4% of the variance in the demand forecasting, inventory optimization and operational efficiency respectively. The results showed that the use of AI-powered technologies was linked to improved supply chain capabilities…

ai.title: Artificial intelligence and classical statistical models for time series forecasting: a comprehensive review
ai.authors: Essam Halim Houssein, Meran Mohamed, Eman M. G. Younis et al.
ai.abstract: Time series forecasting plays a critical role in decision-making across diverse domains such as finance, healthcare, and environmental monitoring. While classical statistical models like ARIMA remain interpretable and efficient, they often struggle with nonlinear patterns and dynamic dependencies. This review systematically examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and optimization techniques enhance forecasting accuracy and robustness. We evaluate modern deep learning architectures (e.g., LSTM, GRU, Transformers), hybrid frameworks (e.g., VMD-LSTM, CNN-GRU), and optimization-augmented models. A meta-analysis of over 150 studies reveals that deep learning-based approaches, particularly those enhanced with Adam and RMSProp optimizers, improve forecasting accuracy by up to 14% compared to traditional methods. Hybrid models demonstrate superior performance in multi-step predictions and handling volatility. The analysis includes financial datasets (S&P 500, NASDAQ) and environmental data (Beijing $$PM_{2.5}$$ ). Despite their power, AI-driven models face challenges including interpretability, computational cost, and data dependency. Future directions highlight explainable AI, transfer learning, and lightweight architectures to address these limitations. This work serves as a reference for researchers exploring the evolving landscape of time series forecasting through AI and…

ai.title: Predictive Analytics in Supply Chain Management: The Role of AI and Machine Learning in Demand Forecasting
ai.authors: Uma Shankar G V Radhakrishnan
ai.venue: Journal of Informatics Education and Research
ai.abstract: Predictive analytics has emerged as a transformative approach in supply chain management (SCM), significantly enhancing efficiency, accuracy, and adaptability. This study explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies in demand forecasting, a critical component of SCM. The study highlights how AI and ML algorithms can process vast datasets, identify patterns, and deliver precise demand forecasts, enabling businesses to optimize inventory levels, reduce waste, and enhance customer satisfaction. Key AI and ML techniques, such as neural networks, support vector machines, and deep learning, are examined for their contributions to improving predictive accuracy in dynamic market conditions. The paper also delves into real-world applications, including demand-supply balancing, seasonal trend analysis, and anomaly detection, demonstrating how organizations leverage these technologies to achieve a competitive edge. Additionally, the research addresses challenges such as data quality, algorithmic biases, and the need for skilled personnel to manage AI-driven systems. Ethical considerations and the importance of maintaining transparency in AI-based decision-making processes are also discussed. The review emphasizes the potential of AI and ML to revolutionize demand forecasting by making supply chains more responsive and resilient. In…

ai.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for predictive supply chain management, focus on how AI- driven tools are revolutionizing demand forecasting and inventory optimization
ai.authors: Uche Nweje, Moyosore Taiwo
ai.venue: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
ai.abstract: The dynamic landscape of global supply chains necessitates innovative solutions to tackle challenges in demand forecasting and inventory optimization. Traditional methods, often constrained by limited adaptability and scalability, struggle to manage the complexities of modern supply chains. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force, enabling predictive supply chain management through advanced data analytics, machine learning algorithms, and real-time decision-making capabilities. By harnessing AI-driven tools, businesses can accurately forecast demand patterns, reduce stockouts, and minimize excess inventory, thereby improving operational efficiency and customer satisfaction. AI-powered systems leverage historical data, market trends, and external factors such as economic shifts and weather conditions to provide precise predictions. These tools enhance responsiveness by identifying potential disruptions and enabling proactive measures, ensuring supply chain resilience. Furthermore, AI facilitates seamless integration across supply chain nodes, fostering collaboration and enabling data-driven insights that were previously unattainable. From predictive analytics for demand forecasting to intelligent automation in inventory management, AI-driven tools are revolutionizing the traditional supply chain model. Case studies reveal substantial reductions in…

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Demand Forecasting Models for Enhancing Supply Chain Planning Accuracy in Saudi Industrial Sectors
ai.authors: Samir Ali Syed
ai.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence Engineering and Transformation
ai.abstract: Accurate demand forecasting is a cornerstone of effective supply chain planning; however, traditional forecasting techniques often fail to capture complex market dynamics, nonlinear demand patterns, and rapid environmental changes. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed demand forecasting by enabling advanced learning from large, heterogeneous datasets through machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and hybrid analytical models. Within the context of Saudi Arabia’s industrial sectors—shaped by Vision 2030 objectives of economic diversification, industrial localization, and digital transformation—AI-driven demand forecasting presents a strategic mechanism for improving planning accuracy and operational resilience. This study examines the theoretical foundations, model architectures, implementation considerations, and strategic benefits of AI-based demand forecasting in Saudi industrial supply chains. It further discusses integration with digital platforms, real-time analytics, and multi-source data fusion. A conceptual deployment framework is proposed to demonstrate how AI forecasting can enhance planning accuracy, reduce inventory inefficiencies, and support national supply chain development goals.

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence in Supply Chain Demand Forecasting: A Structured Review of Method Evolution, Context Dependence and Research Gaps
ai.authors: Benchao Zhai
ai.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
ai.abstract: Demand forecasting is at the starting point of the supply chain planning link, and the forecast deviation is amplified along the chain to form a bullwhip effect, causing the backlog and shortage to occur at the same time. Machine learning and deep learning methods have entered this field in large numbers in recent years, but the literature is scattered across settings as different as retail, medicine, fresh produce and spare parts. This article is based on OpenAlex structured search to review: from 2015 to 2026, there are 2,970 records, and after qualifying the sources of journals and conferences, there are 2,227 records, of which 1,210 contain artificial intelligence method terms, and 18 representative studies are deeply synthesized. The results are threefold. The method genealogy progresses along statistical methods, tree models, deep sequence models, attention and hybrid architecture, and 91.9% of attention literature appears in 2024 and later. The statistical method has not been withdrawn. 71.9% of its literature also comes from the past three years, and it remains the main control benchmark. The accuracy advantage of artificial intelligence depends on the demand form. It is stable in continuous high-density scenarios, while the evidence in intermittent demand and truncated observation scenarios is weak. ai.title: STORE SALES PREDICTION USING MACHINE LEARNING, STATISTICAL MODELING AND DEEP LEARNING FRAMEWORKS: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS
ai.authors: Ayesha Awan, asif ahsan, Syed Irteza
ai.abstract: Sales forecasting or prediction is an essential tool for businesses to make informed decisions about resource allocation, budgeting, and marketing strategies. Sales prediction involves predicting future sales of a product or service. There are several methods that businesses can use to forecast sales, including statistical analysis, market research, and expert opinion. Key factors that can impact sales predictions include market conditions, economic trends, competition, and customer behavior. However, forecasting sales can be a challenging tasks, as it require businesses to accurately forecast future demand and predict future sales in the face of changing market conditions and unpredictable customer behavior. There are also several uncertainties that businesses may face when forecasting or predicting sales, such as economic conditions, competition, customer behavior, product life cycles, and external events. In this research, we are doing sales prediction and providing a comparative analysis of three widely used techniques in the field of forecasting, namely: statistical modeling, machine learning, and deep learning. In our analysis, we are using the data given by the Rossmann supply chain, which is the second largest drugstore chain in Europe, and to the best of our knowledge, no one has ever used the deep learning approach to predict sales of these stores. Our study aims to…

ai.title: The Impact of AI On Supply Chain Planning and Demand Forecasting
ai.authors: Sachinkumar Vinodbhai Sadhu, Rajveer Singh Gohil, Dr. Hasmukh Panchal
ai.abstract: This study examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in improving supply chain planning and demand forecasting. With increasing market uncertainty and data complexity, traditional forecasting methods often fail to deliver accurate and timely results. AI-based techniques, especially machine learning and deep learning models, provide better prediction capabilities by analyzing large datasets and identifying hidden patterns. However, the adoption of AI in supply chains is limited due to a lack of transparency and understanding of model outputs. To address this issue, the concept of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is introduced, which helps decision-makers interpret and trust AI-based forecasts. The study uses a quantitative research approach based on secondary data from the FMCG sector. It highlights how AI improves forecasting accuracy, reduces inventory waste, and supports sustainable supply chain practices. The findings suggest that integrating AI with explainability can enhance decision-making, operational efficiency, and environmental performance. The study concludes by proposing a simple framework that combines AI, explainability, and sustainability for better supply chain management in emerging economies like India.

ai.title: Sales Forecasting Using Machine Learning
ai.authors: Shivam Agrahari
ai.venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
ai.abstract: Abstract—(1)Sales forecasting is a critical component of business strategy and inventory management, enabling organizations to make informed decisions based on future market demand. (2)This research explores the application of machine learning algorithms for improving the accuracy and efficiency of sales forecasting. (3)By analyzing historical sales data, external factors such as seasonal trends, promotions, and economic indicators, the study implements and evaluates various machine learning models including Linear Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks. (4)The comparative analysis reveals that advanced models like LSTM outperform traditional statistical methods by capturing temporal dependencies and nonlinear patterns in the data. (5)The study also integrates data preprocessing techniques, feature engineering, and model tuning to enhance prediction performance. (6)Experimental results demonstrate that machine learning-based forecasting not only improves accuracy but also enables dynamic, real-time adaptability for businesses. (7)This work contributes to the growing body of knowledge on AI-driven decision-making, paving the way for smarter, data-informed business operations. Keywords— sales forecasting, machine learning, LSTM, time series, regression, inventory management, demand prediction, business intelligence.

ai.authors: Adebimpe Omolayo Esan, Oluwasogo Daodu, Nnamdi Stephen Okomba et al.
ai.venue: Faculty of Natural and Applied Sciences Journal of Computing and Applications
ai.abstract: Sales forecasting is a critical activity for businesses, enabling them to make informed decisions about production, inventory, marketing, and other key areas. Traditional sales forecasting methods, such as time series analysis and statistical regression, are often unable to capture the complex relationships between factors influencing sales, leading to potential inaccuracies. This study aims to address these limitations by developing a sales forecasting model using deep learning and machine learning techniques. Deep learning methods, capable of modeling complex relationships and adapting to changing market conditions, are expected to improve the accuracy and cost-effectiveness of sales forecasting. This study involves data collection and preprocessing, model development and evaluation. LSTM model, performed quite well with an accuracy of approximately 80%. The Random Forest Regressor and XGB Regressor outperformed the LSTM model with accuracy scores of 94.79% and 98.7% respectively. On the other hand, the Linear Regressor model underperformed, delivering an accuracy of just 57.72%. This study reinforces the idea that a combination of traditional forecasting methods, machine learning, and deep learning models can be utilized effectively to gain more accurate sales forecasts. ai.title: AI/ML-Based Demand Forecasting Across Industries: Transforming Traditional Sales Prediction Through Advanced Analytics
ai.authors: Balusamy Chinnappaiyan
ai.venue: Journal of Information Systems Engineering & Management
ai.abstract: Demand forecasting is a strategic discipline that anticipates future customer demand, enabling organizations to align production, inventory, and capacity decisions with market needs to drive profitability and competitive advantage. Traditional statistical methods have served organizations for decades, relying primarily on historical sales patterns and time-series analysis to generate predictions. However, contemporary business environments characterized by unprecedented demand volatility, rapidly shifting consumer preferences, and complex market dynamics have exposed significant limitations in conventional forecasting approaches. Artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies offer transformative capabilities that address these challenges through multi-source data integration, pattern recognition across vast datasets, and adaptive learning mechanisms that respond to changing market conditions in real-time. This review examines the evolution from traditional statistical forecasting to AI-powered demand prediction systems, with primary emphasis on retail sector implementations where inventory optimization and sales forecasting directly impact profitability margins. Healthcare organizations utilize similar technologies to forecast medical supply requirements and patient volume patterns, ensuring adequate resource availability while minimizing waste. Manufacturing…

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mathematical Modeling of Complex Systems: A Comprehensive Review of Concepts, Applications, and Future Directions
ai.authors: Dhruvika Jadav, Tushar Mandanaka
ai.venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
ai.abstract: This paper investigates how to include artificial intelligence (AI) methods into complex system mathematical modelling. Traditionally, techniques like system dynamics, network theory, and algebraic modelling are used to study complex systems, which are distinguished by dynamic interactions, nonlinear behaviour, and high dimensionality. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), namely machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has created new possibilities for improving forecast accuracy, revealing latent patterns, and allowing adaptive behaviour in these systems. Because AI algorithms are so good at learning from massive amounts of data, they may be used for time series forecasting, anomaly detection, optimisation, and decision-making. In fields like image and speech recognition, bioinformatics, and autonomous systems, neural network models—which are essential to machine learning and deep learning—have shown an amazing capacity to represent and analyse complicated phenomena. Additionally, the integration of data-driven modelling with conventional theoretical frameworks improves the capacity to capture system behaviours that are challenging to represent analytically. Complex system optimisation and self-regulation are further supported by AI-enabled adaptive control systems. In conclusion, combining AI and mathematical modelling enhances simulation accuracy while…

ai.title: Deep Learning for Time Series Forecasting: Review and Applications in Geotechnics and Geosciences
ai.authors: Farid Fazel Mojtahedi, Negin Yousefpour, Shiao Huey Chow et al.
ai.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
ai.abstract: This paper presents a detailed review of existing and emerging deep learning algorithms for time series forecasting in geotechnics and geoscience applications. Deep learning has shown promising results in addressing complex prediction problems involving large datasets and multiple interacting variables without requiring extensive feature extraction. This study provides an in-depth description of prominent deep learning methods, including recurrent neural networks (RNNs), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), generative adversarial network, deep belief network, reinforcement learning, attention and transformer algorithms as well as hybrid networks using a combination of these architectures. In addition, this paper summarizes the applications of these models in various fields, including mining and tunnelling, railway and road construction, seismology, slope stability, earth retaining and stabilizing structures, remote sensing, as well as scour and erosion. This review reveals that RNN-based models, particularly Long Short-Term Memory networks, are the most commonly used models for time series forecasting. The advantages of deep learning models over traditional machine learning, including their superior ability to handle complex patterns and process large-scale data more effectively, are discussed. ai.title: Evolution and impact of artificial intelligence in sustainable supply chain management: Systematic review and bibliometric analysis
ai.authors: Sara Ghouati, Salah Oulfarsi, Adil El Amri
ai.abstract: This study analyzes the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in supply chain management through a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of 292 articles (2020–2023) from Scopus. It examines three areas: the evolution of research (RQ1), the impact of AI on processes (RQ2), and its strategic influence (RQ3). The results reveal that machine learning (16 studies) and deep learning (seven studies) dominate, optimizing demand forecasting and inventory management (Rana & Daultani, 2023). Sectors such as the food industry are benefiting from waste reductions thanks to AI (Kumar et al., 2021), while the automotive industry is improving predictive maintenance (Dumitrascu et al., 2020). However, challenges persist: lack of empirical validation, algorithmic biases, and difficulties with adoption by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) (Fosso Wamba, 2022). Strategically, AI strengthens the resilience of supply chains (Christopher & Holweg, 2017), but its hybrid potential (e.g., AI + blockchain) remains underexploited (Arunmozhi et al., 2022). Theoretical implications highlight the need for dynamic models that integrate socioeconomic criteria, while practitioners must adapt AI to specific industry circumstances. This study provides valuable insights to guide researchers and practitioners in leveraging AI technologies to improve supply chain efficiency, resilience, and…

ai.venue: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
ai.abstract: Accurate sales forecasting is a critical driver for strategic decision-making, inventory optimization, and supply chain efficiency in modern retail and corporate environments. While traditional statistical methods like ARIMA and exponential smoothing excel at capturing linear patterns, they often struggle with the highly volatile, non-linear, and multi-variable nature of contemporary market data. This paper explores the application of advanced deep learning architectures for time series analysis to enhance sales prediction accuracy. We investigate and compare the performance of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), and Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) alongside modern Transformer-based models. These deep learning frameworks are uniquely capable of automatically feature-engineering complex temporal dependencies, seasonal fluctuations, and promotional impacts from massive historical datasets without requiring manual lag selection. By integrating exogenous variables such as economic indicators, pricing strategies, marketing campaigns, and regional holidays, these models achieve superior generalization over longer forecasting horizons. ai.title: Research on Supply Chain Logistics Prediction and Decision Optimization Driven by Artificial Intelligence
ai.authors: Shubing Chen
ai.abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, its application in supply chain management has gradually become an important means to improve efficiency and optimize decision-making. This study focuses on supply chain logistics prediction and decision optimization driven by artificial intelligence, analyzing the application of artificial intelligence technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, and data mining in the logistics field. Through research on demand forecasting, inventory management, transportation scheduling, and other aspects, this article finds that artificial intelligence can effectively improve the accuracy of forecasting, optimize the decision-making process, thereby reducing costs, improving response speed, and enhancing the flexibility of the supply chain. At the same time, this study also explores the challenges faced in practical applications, such as data quality, system integration, and technical costs, and proposes corresponding solutions. Finally, this paper looks forward to the development trend of artificial intelligence in future supply chain logistics management, and believes that with the further maturity of technology, artificial intelligence will play an increasingly important role in various links of the supply chain.

ai.title: Comprehensive review of artificial intelligence applications in renewable energy systems: current implementations and emerging trends
ai.authors: Chukwuebuka Joseph Ejiyi, Dongsheng Cai, D. A. H. Thomas et al.
ai.abstract: As the world faces pressing climate and energy challenges, Artificial Intelligence is proven as a transformative force in advancing renewable energy systems. This study reviews the current and future applications of Artificial Intelligence in renewable energy, highlighting its transformative role in enhancing the efficiency, reliability, and scalability of renewable energy systems. The study draws from over 400 recent publications, selected based on their relevance to Artificial Intelligence and renewable energy systems. We discuss the use of Artificial Intelligence techniques including machine learning, deep learning, and reinforcement learning models for optimizing energy production, forecasting demand, predictive maintenance, and managing decentralized energy systems. Emerging fields such as quantum machine learning and Artificial Intelligence-augmented reality are also considered because of their potential to transform energy infrastructures. The survey reviews significant innovations in wind and solar energy, energy storage, and smart grid technologies, focusing on how Artificial Intelligence addresses challenges like intermittency and variability. Furthermore, we discuss the importance of big data, the Internet of Things, and real-time analytics in advancing Artificial Intelligence models, along with the evolving landscape of Artificial Intelligence-driven policy and…

ai.title: Forecast Value Add: Reward-Based Action Selection over Probabilistic Demand Forecasts
ai.authors: Ankur Verma
ai.abstract: Strong machine-learning ensembles capture much of the trend, seasonality, and known events in demand, yet they can still understate peaks, miss moving events, or mistake temporary changes for shifts in demand level. We address this gap by framing forecast refinement as a reward-driven decision problem. For each forecast period, we let an agent choose among values already produced by the ensemble: its base forecast, distribution-free bounds, quantiles, and a bias-corrected estimate. We evaluate these choices against context-matched historical periods, accounting for calendar position, recurring and moving events, trend, price, and promotions. We then apply a structural seasonal guard to constrain adjustments and record the model, agent, and planner contributions to every published value. We evaluate our approach across five retail, consumer-goods, and direct-to-consumer deployments over nine months. Our refined forecasts reduce mean WMAPE by 6.3% compared with the stacked machine-learning forecast for every customer, with gains reaching 16.7%, and achieve the lowest error in 35 of 45 customer-months. Compared with statistical forecasts, our approach reduces mean error by 18.7%. These results demonstrate that context-aware, auditable action selection can add forecast value beyond a strong ensemble.

ai.title: Conformal Prediction for Multi-Step Forecasting: Conditional Coverage and Sharp Score Calibration Rates
ai.authors: Siyuan He, Yuhong Yang
ai.abstract: Uncertainty quantification in prediction is a central problem in statistics and machine learning. Conformal prediction provides a flexible approach to constructing prediction sets with valid marginal coverage under exchangeability. In this paper, we investigate conformal prediction for both one-step and multi-step forecasting from a single stationary time series, addressing temporal dependence and the additional challenges of joint prediction across multiple horizons. We propose a kernel-based framework, called Time series Residual Analysis for Calibration with Kernels (TRACK), for estimating conditional quantiles of residual scores and constructing prediction sets from rolling-window forecasters. The framework accommodates heterogeneous uncertainty across horizons and accounts for dependence induced by rolling estimation, while allowing predictor memory and forecast horizons to grow with the sample size. Our finite-sample bounds quantify how temporal dependence and overlapping score windows affect calibration and coverage. We further derive bounds for conditional quantile estimation and pointwise conditional coverage discrepancy. The guarantees extend to more general predictors that admit an accurate rolling-window approximation. We also derive matching minimax bounds over classes of known score maps, clarifying how overlapping score windows affect calibration accuracy.…

ai.title: TimeHF 2.0: Multimodal, Multivariate, and Multi-Region Collaborative Forecasting for Large-Scale Retail Supply Chains
ai.authors: Zhongxuan Han, Zhengxin Shi, Kunxiu Chen et al.
ai.abstract: Large-scale retail supply chains need sales forecasts for specified products, future dates or planning windows, and regions under the conditions available at the forecast origin. Regional sparsity, changing environments, volatile sales, and unfamiliar business situations make these dimensions difficult to model together. We introduce TimeHF 2.0, a multimodal, multivariate, and multi-region collaborative forecasting framework that makes flexibly expressed business knowledge usable in numerical prediction. A coverage-aware directed encoder integrates regional sales and applicable covariates. A semantic alignment module transfers language-model hidden representations of natural-language plans and domain experience into target-specific forecasting context. Learning against sales observations connects these meanings to numerical evidence, allowing business users to supply experience, future plans, and changing circumstances without defining a new numerical feature for each description. Text-conditioned future queries and shared/routed experts adapt prediction to the supplied context. An ordered-distribution head allocates fine resolution to routine fluctuations and coarse resolution to extreme sales movements, while daily/window learning connects forecasts to cumulative planning quantities. Online parallel forecasting at JD yields relative accuracy improvements of 18.25% and 17.94%…

ai.title: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events
ai.authors: Huajian Zhang, Mingyue Cheng, Xingpeng Gao et al.
ai.abstract: Accurate electricity load forecasting provides critical decision support for energy procurement, generation scheduling, and supply-demand balancing, contributing to the economic efficiency and operational reliability of power systems. However, future electricity demand can be affected by the complex interplay of multiple events described in Web notices, weather alerts, and event schedules. Their effects vary over time and can reinforce or offset one another, making electricity load difficult to forecast accurately. While existing methods can incorporate context as additional input, how to use the effects of multiple events and their interactions to guide the load forecasting process itself remains to be explored. To address this gap, we propose ElecLoad, a context-aware agent for multi-event electricity load forecasting that adaptively organizes the forecasting process. Specifically, we train ElecLoad to combine historical load with context to analyze each event's relevance to the target load, the timing of its effects, and potential interactions among events. Guided by this analysis, ElecLoad adaptively chooses to forecast the entire forecast horizon directly or to partition it into segments according to changes in event effects. When the horizon is partitioned, sub-agents independently generate initial forecasts for each segment. The main agent then reviews these forecasts,…

ai.title: Aggregate Calibration Can Mask Stress-State Undercoverage: Bounded-Memory Forecast Intervals under Recurrent Financial Stress
ai.authors: Ruihang Han, Li-Hsiang Lin
ai.abstract: Sequential forecast intervals are often evaluated by aggregate coverage even when calibration memory is bounded. This can be misleading when economically important states recur after long absences: a recent-only buffer may satisfy its overall coverage target while no longer containing errors from earlier episodes of the returning state. We study this problem in next-day financial range forecasting, holding the forecasting model, conformity score, adaptive update, and memory budget constant while varying the historical residual information available at each query. Recent-only first-in, first-out (FIFO) calibration is near nominal in aggregate but undercovers substantially during high-volatility states in both an exchange-traded fund development panel and a fixed stock panel. An unbounded state-history reference yields a lower observed stress-period interval score; Rare replay yields lower high-VIX interval scores than the matched Recent-n and Hybrid-n controls in both panels, and the state-structured versus recent-only contrast is largest near stress re-entry. Bounded calibration memory is therefore part of the forecasting information design, and aggregate calibration alone can conceal state-specific reliability failures.

ai.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
ai.authors: Abdul Fatir Ansari, Oleksandr Shchur, Jaris Küken et al.
ai.abstract: Accurate forecasting with uncertainty quantification is critical in a variety of scientific applications ranging from epidemiology and economics to energy systems and earth sciences. Yet most forecasting models still need to be developed and trained separately for each domain-specific dataset. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to remove this limitation and enable the application of the same model across domains through large-scale pretraining. However, most existing TSFMs treat each time series independently and therefore cannot model interactions among time series and external drivers. Here, we introduce Chronos-2, a foundation model for zero-shot forecasting that models the interactions between multivariate time series and heterogeneous covariates, which commonly arise in scientific applications. The model infers relationships among time series directly from historical context and generates probabilistic forecasts without task-specific treatment. Across various benchmarks, Chronos-2 achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on average by improving skill scores by 5.2 percentage points relative to the strongest baselines and increasing win rates by 10 percentage points. Chronos-2 is also computationally efficient, generating forecasts for 100 time series in under one second on a single mid-range GPU, 50x and 1000x faster end-to-end than the best task-specific point and…

ai.title: Fuzzy selective state model for forecasting the dynamics of consumer preferences
ai.authors: P. A. Golovinski, A. A. Drobyshev, A. O. Shatalova
ai.abstract: We consider forecasting the dynamics of consumer preferences of retail chain customers. A customer's preference is described by a triangular fuzzy number. The evolution of the preference over time is governed by a Mamba-type selective state space model whose hidden state is a triangular number, with computations carried out in M.G.~Matveev's two-component algebra of fuzzy numbers. The recurrence parameters are computed from crisp features, while the fuzzy part of the model remains linear with non-negative coefficients. We show that the state then always remains a proper triangular number and is a convex combination of past observations, so that the fuzziness of the forecast does not accumulate over time and the algebraic computations coincide with Zadeh's extension principle. On a synthetic example with competitor promotions and customer switching, a lightweight 107-parameter model reaches a mean absolute error of the forecast centre of 0.154 versus 0.163 for the constant-inertia evolution operator and 0.179 for the naive forecast, matches a crisp model of the same architecture and additionally provides a linguistically interpretable estimate of forecast vagueness. We also show how the linguistic readout of the forecast can be used to detect a permanent switch of a customer to a competitor.

ai.title: FARE: Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion for Retail Forecasting
ai.authors: Chenghao Gu, Zhuokang Shen, Shenghao Wu et al.
ai.abstract: Retail sales forecasting underpins inventory planning, yet promotions and calendar events reshape short-term demand. Although each factor usually has historical occurrences, the complete factor combination of a target week often has few precedents. The challenge is therefore to retrieve informative partial matches and weight them by their reliability, which varies across series. We propose FARE(Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion), which ranks historical weeks separately for each known target-week factor and merges the selected weeks into a factor reference under a fixed budget. Guided by shrunk errors from completed development weeks and the current disagreement among candidates, a first gate mixes this factor reference with a shape reference from similar sales histories, and a second gate controls how strongly the mixture corrects a backbone forecast. Both gates remain fixed during testing. On Favorita, M5, Rossmann, and Rohlik, FARE reduces the weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE) of five backbones by 11.46%, 4.06%, 14.63%, and 10.16% on average. With Chronos-2 frozen, FARE also outperforms conventional and existing enhancement methods, including supervised residual correction and retrieval augmentation. Code is available at https://github.com/HousonGu/FARE .

ai.title: A Deep Learning Framework for Quantile Demand Forecasting in E-commerce with Doubly Censored Data
ai.authors: Ziwen Ye, Jiawen Wei, Teng Song et al.
ai.abstract: In recent years, a growing number of online retail companies have embraced deep learning models for demand forecasting, leveraging their scalability in processing large-scale datasets. Accurate demand forecasts enable improved planning and allow operational flexibility to adjust sales accordingly. Moreover, quantile estimation has gained widespread application as it offers valuable uncertainty quantification, thereby enhancing the robustness of decision-making processes. However, limited research has addressed the effective quantification of uncertainty when target labels are ambiguous. In retail, actual sales can be capped by stock and boosted by temporary promotions, whereas the target is underlying demand. Such scenarios are characterized by double censoring and no deep-learning pipeline yet exists for such data. In this paper, we introduce a straightforward framework for learning quantiles from doubly-censored observations and propose a tailored evaluation metric. Our approach is supported by theoretical guarantees, and we empirically demonstrate that our metric correlates well with the oracle calibration measure. Experimental results show that our estimator surpasses existing baselines. Finally, inventory simulations and real-world applications confirm the practical utility of our method in retail operations.

ai.title: Vendster: An Evaluation Arena to Investigate How Forecasting Tool Quality Affects LLM Agent Behaviors in Buyer-Vendor Negotiation
ai.authors: Charin Polpanumas
ai.abstract: Time-series forecasters are ranked almost entirely by accuracy metrics, but a forecast's decision value, its effect on the downstream decision, need not track accuracy and is rarely measured. This problem compounds as large language model (LLM) agents increasingly consume forecasters as tools, mediating them through stochastic, opaque policies. We present Vendster, an evaluation arena measuring how a forecaster's bias and prediction-interval width change the outcome of a buyer--vendor discount negotiation between two LLM agents. In the reference instance Vendster-M5, sampling base demand patterns from the M5 dataset, we evaluate two frontier-closed LLM families (Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.6 Sol) and two open ones (DeepSeek-V3.2 and Qwen3-235B-A22B). Model-generated forecasts raise sales target attainment by up to +17 percentage points (p<0.001), yet standard forecast evaluation metrics such as relWQL and MASE do not predict negotiation outcomes at a statistically significant level. To isolate the causal structure, we substitute in synthetic forecasts with controlled bias and interval width. Under-prediction bias significantly improves outcomes for agents that react more to the forecasts---dose-response slopes -0.387 and -0.416 (p<0.001). Interval width has no statistically significant effect at zero bias. These findings indicate that the direction of forecast bias and agent…

ai.title: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Adaptive Forecasting from Heterogeneous Evidence
ai.authors: Madumita Karthikeyan, Umang Rajnikant Bid, Rong Pan
ai.abstract: Real-world forecasting often requires integrating heterogeneous evidence whose predictive value varies across horizons, operating regimes, and domains. We introduce FACTS-MAS, a domain-agnostic multi-agent forecasting framework that decomposes evidence into specialized channels for temporal dynamics, exogenous context, seasonality, structural information, and discrete events. Each agent generates an independently testable forecast through a common interface, while leakage-safe historical validation measures its predictive skill relative to a naive reference. These skill estimates are used to weight and combine agent forecasts, so that uninformative evidence is either removed or downweighted rather than forced to participate. A calibration procedure selects domain-specific constant means based on historical validation folds. We evaluate FACTS-MAS on weekly for-sale housing inventory from Zillow and weekly unemployment insurance claims from FRED, for 15 U.S. metropolitan areas at 4-, 8-, and 13-week forecasting horizons. Our method outperforms both a naive last-value forecast method and the TimesFM foundation model. However, a factor-adjusted exponential smoothing model performs as well as the fused forecast. The evidence therefore supports FACTS-MAS as a systematic protocol for testing, calibrating, and recomposing evidence channels before assembling them into the strongest…

ai.title: Efficient probabilistic weather forecasting at quarter-degree resolution with two-sided transport attention
ai.authors: Junu Choi, Youngjoon Hong
ai.abstract: High-resolution probabilistic weather forecasting remains computationally demanding. Here we present Astra, a 0.25$^\circ$ ensemble model trained on eight H200 GPUs. It combines Kantorovich Attention, a two-sided transport attention in which each region chooses where it reads from and writes to, so every region sends and receives at token resolution, with a self-featurised continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) that also scores forecasts in the model's multiscale features. In WeatherBench 2, Astra matches GenCast's CRPS averaged over five upper-air targets and days 1-10 with 9.8% of its hardware-normalised training compute. Verified against ERA5, its CRPS and ensemble-mean root-mean-square error are lower than the ECMWF ensemble's on all 600 variable, level and lead-time combinations, and its CRPS is lower than GenCast's on 73.5% of them. A 15-day member needs 39 times fewer floating-point operations than GenCast's GPU implementation, and 50 members take under 40 min on one consumer GPU, within 21 GB.

logistics.title: Research on Supply Chain Management of Costco
logistics.venue: Frontiers in Business Economics and Management
logistics.abstract: As the world's largest warehouse membership retailer, Costco's successful operation and management model has attracted much attention. This paper conducts an in-depth study on Costco's operation and management model, and analyzes its characteristics and advantages in supply chain management, inventory management, logistics management, and employee management. The research results show that Costco's operation and management model is centered on efficient supply chain management, lean inventory management, flexible logistics management, and motivated employee management, achieving low-cost and high-efficiency operations. At the same time, this paper also explores the replicability and limitations of Costco's operation and management model, providing reference and reference for other companies.

logistics.title: Operations at Flipkart Supply Chain Management
logistics.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
logistics.abstract: This research paper explores the operations of Flipkart's supply chain management system, focusing on its structure, strategies, and technological innovations. As one of India's largest e-commerce platforms, Flipkart has built a highly responsive and efficient supply chain network to handle vast product assortments, fluctuating demand, and complex logistics. This paper aims to analyze how Flipkart manages procurement, inventory, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery while maintaining customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. The study also sheds light on the company's sustainability initiatives and the future of e-commerce logistics in India

logistics.title: SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT PRACTICES AND THEIR IMPACT ON OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY IN RETAIL ENTERPRISES
logistics.venue: Manuscript on Sustainable Economics Finance and Management
logistics.abstract: Effective supply chain management (SCM) is increasingly critical to the competitiveness and operational efficiency of retail enterprises. This study examines how SCM practices procurement processes, inventory management, supplier collaboration, logistics & distribution, and information systems influence operational efficiency in organized retail in Karnataka. Adopting a mixed-methods approach, the study draws on a structured survey of 400 store managers/operations staff across five Karnataka cities (Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubli–Dharwad, Belagavi) and 15 in-depth interviews with supply-chain managers and suppliers. Quantitative analysis uses descriptive statistics, ANOVA, and multiple regression; qualitative data were analysed by thematic coding. Results indicate that improved inventory management (higher inventory turnover, lower stockouts), integrated IT systems (real-time inventory visibility), and closer supplier collaboration (joint planning, vendor-managed inventory pilots) significantly predict higher operational efficiency (measured via order fulfilment rate, reduced lead time, and lower supply-chain cost per sale). logistics.title: ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF AI-AUTOMATION IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT
logistics.abstract: Artificial intelligence nowadays stands among the most powerful transformative forces of modern times for supply chain management. It opens a new avenue towards automation, optimization, and better decision-making. This dissertation seeks to explore how AI-driven automation impacts supply chain processes in an industrial context with respect to influences on operational performance, inventory control, and stock optimization. The study therefore has a mixed-methods character, as it encompasses not only quantitative data from questionnaires, but also qualitative insights provided through in-depth interviews with professionals across diverse industries-manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, among others. Results indicate that AI technologies like predictive analytics and machine learning algorithms with robotic process automation enhance efficiency in supply chains, reduce costs, and make better decisions. This study also attempts to make a case for the presence of major challenges, including technical integration problems, an initial high cost, and lack of confidencea in data privacy. logistics.abstract: Industry 4.0 has revolutionized supply chain management and logistics through a concentration on automation, data interchange, and smart technologies. Furthermore, by maximizing the usage of resources and minimizing negative environmental effects, AMRs play a crucial role in promoting resilience and sustainability. logistics.abstract: Background: Efficient Supply Chain Management (SCM) is critical for ensuring timely and safe surgical care, particularly in resource-constrained settings. logistics.abstract: This paper examines the current level of implementing machine learning and deep learning to meet the challenges and needs of supply chain management. Machine learning and deep learning have been instrumental in revolutionizing decision-making and enhancing the performance of supply chain management operations. While global systems of supply chain continue to become complex, machine learning and deep learning afford appreciable paradigms to deal with issues like demand forecast, inventory control and logistics management. This work analyzes 43 selected peer-reviewed papers and case studies on machine learning and deep learning in supply chain management, having in mind fundamental algorithms that include neural networks, CNNs and reinforcement learning. It discusses how big data sources and predictive analytics models are used to combine real-time decision-making into supply chain management systems. These technologies enable enhancements in the way that data is preprocessed and predictions. Self-organization has the potential to manage risks within a supply chain. A survey research design was adopted for this study. The target population included employees from local e-commerce platforms, last-mile delivery providers, third-party logistics (3PL) firms, warehouse operators, and related stakeholders such as fulfillment centers and order management units. A sample of 200 respondents was randomly selected to ensure representation across different functions in the e-commerce supply chain. Three research questions and corresponding hypotheses were developed to guide the study. A four-point Likert-type questionnaire was employed to collect primary data. The data were analyzed using Pearson product-moment correlation to test the hypotheses. The findings revealed that major bottlenecks experienced by e-commerce businesses in logistics and supply chain operations were primarily due to the absence of appropriate logistics models that could streamline and optimize delivery, inventory, and fulfillment processes. Furthermore, the study found a significant lack of quantitative and empirical approaches in decision-making and problem-solving activities across many e-commerce logistics functions. logistics.title: Optimization of last-mile delivery in KSA

This study has demonstrated the importance of optimizing the last-mile delivery process for logistics companies in Taif city to enhance their competitiveness and meet the growing demand to achieve customer's satisfaction. The research found that logistics companies in Saudi Arabia struggle to meet customer demand on time while maintaining cost-efficiency. A survey of logistics customers and a case study of one Logistics Company supported this conclusion. The study identified the lack of proper routing planning as the main cause of delays and developed a mathematical model and a Python program to address this issue. By implementing these solutions, we were able to find feasible solutions to the challenges faced by logistics companies, including optimizing the delivery routes and reducing transportation costs. The mathematical model and the Python program provided feasible solutions that reduced the total distance traveled by delivery vehicles by 17.21% and 162 km, respectively, resulting in significant cost and timesaving. The study demonstrates that optimizing delivery processes can significantly improve the efficiency and reliability of operations and reduce fuel costs. logistics.title: Trends in AI-Based Supply Chain Management: A Text Mining Analysis of Academic Literature
logistics.abstract: This study examines research trends in the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and its impacts within the field of supply chain management (SCM). A total of 1,663 academic articles published since 2000 that investigate AI applications in SCM were analyzed using network text analysis and topic modeling techniques. The results reveal that the integration of AI into supply chain management has generated positive effects on traditional supply chain performance indicators, such as improved demand forecasting accuracy and enhanced inventory and logistics management. In addition, AI adoption has shown significant implications for supply chain sustainability and resilience. The analysis identifies four major research topic groups associated with AI-based supply chain management: (1) core technologies, (2) sustainability enhancement, (3) resilience building, and (4) security and ethical issues. By systematically structuring the existing body of research, this study provides a comprehensive overview of the evolving AI-SCM research landscape and offers directions for future research.

logistics.title: APPLICATION OF MATHEMATICAL MODELING IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: A REVIEW
logistics.authors: Norazryana Mat Dawi, Mohammad Akhtar, HAMIDREZA NAMAZI
logistics.abstract: Mathematical modeling plays a critical role in modern supply chain management (SCM) by enabling optimization, forecasting, and informed decision-making across complex networks. This review synthesizes recent advancements in mathematical modeling across five key domains of SCM: demand forecasting, inventory control, logistics and distribution, sustainability, and the integration of emerging technologies. We explore a wide array of modeling techniques, including time-series analysis, stochastic models, optimization algorithms, and machine learning, highlighting their applications, strengths, and limitations. Special attention is given to the evolving roles of artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twins in enhancing model responsiveness and adaptability. Despite these advancements, challenges remain in achieving model transparency, scalability, and seamless integration with real-time technologies such as IoT and digital twins. Future research should focus on developing more interpretable machine learning models, improving data governance, and fostering cross-domain collaboration to enhance decision-making across the supply chain. This review provides a foundational understanding while identifying key gaps and future pathways for innovation in mathematical modeling for supply chain management.

logistics.title: The Impact of Using AI in Supply Chain on Corporate Management
logistics.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
logistics.abstract: As the current market becomes increasingly competitive and labor costs continue to rise, enterprises must explore alternative strategies to enhance their supply chain management for better development and innovation. The main study in this research paper is the potential impact of AI on improving supply chain efficiency. Key components of the supply chain include information processing, inventory management, logistics management and customer feedback. This study focuses on the practical applications of existing AI technologies in supply chain management. The main features are to fasten and animate order data processing, improve order accuracy, simplify and accelerate inventory processes, optimize express delivery routes, and improve customer satisfaction. In addition, AI applications in supply chain management can significantly reduce work time costs and reduce labor costs, enabling companies to develop rapidly and gain a competitive edge in the market.

logistics.title: Differentiable Agent-Based Modeling for Multi-Echelon Supply Chains: Gradient-Based Optimization of Heterogeneous Policies at Scale
logistics.authors: Bulent Soykan, Murtadha Alsayegh, Sean Mondesire et al.
logistics.abstract: Global supply chains rely on the interactions of thousands of heterogeneous agents, posing significant challenges for optimization. While traditional optimization often assumes homogeneity to ensure tractability, Reinforcement Learning struggles with sample inefficiency when scaling to high-dimensional state spaces. We propose a Differentiable Agent-Based Model for multi-echelon inventory management. By implementing stochastic dynamics via differentiable tensor operations, we enable direct gradient propagation through the simulation. We validate the framework by recovering theoretical Newsvendor optima without supervision. Crucially, we demonstrate ``Mass Personalization'' by optimizing 10,000 distinct agent policies simultaneously in seconds, achieving a 53% cost reduction compared to scalar baselines. Furthermore, we utilize gradient sensitivity analysis to generate causal heatmaps, accurately recovering inherent lead-time delays from the computation graph. This approach bridges the gap between simulation and optimization, enabling the efficient training of self-correcting Digital Twins.

logistics.title: TimeHF 2.0: Multimodal, Multivariate, and Multi-Region Collaborative Forecasting for Large-Scale Retail Supply Chains
logistics.authors: Zhongxuan Han, Zhengxin Shi, Kunxiu Chen et al.
logistics.abstract: Large-scale retail supply chains need sales forecasts for specified products, future dates or planning windows, and regions under the conditions available at the forecast origin. Regional sparsity, changing environments, volatile sales, and unfamiliar business situations make these dimensions difficult to model together. We introduce TimeHF 2.0, a multimodal, multivariate, and multi-region collaborative forecasting framework that makes flexibly expressed business knowledge usable in numerical prediction. A coverage-aware directed encoder integrates regional sales and applicable covariates. A semantic alignment module transfers language-model hidden representations of natural-language plans and domain experience into target-specific forecasting context. Learning against sales observations connects these meanings to numerical evidence, allowing business users to supply experience, future plans, and changing circumstances without defining a new numerical feature for each description. Text-conditioned future queries and shared/routed experts adapt prediction to the supplied context. An ordered-distribution head allocates fine resolution to routine fluctuations and coarse resolution to extreme sales movements, while daily/window learning connects forecasts to cumulative planning quantities. Online parallel forecasting at JD yields relative accuracy improvements of 18.25% and 17.94%…

logistics.title: LLM-Based Feature Extraction for Multi-Criteria Inventory Classification
logistics.abstract: E-commerce supply chains generate large volumes of customer feedback and operational data that remain underutilized in inventory management. Traditional inventory classification techniques such as ABC analysis rely primarily on annual dollar usage, while multi-criteria inventory classification (MCIC) methods extend this but still depend on structured quantitative data and do not utilize unstructured information available in modern supply chains. This paper proposes an LLM-based feature extraction approach that transforms unstructured sources such as customer reviews into quantitative features using vector embeddings and LLM-generated evaluation criteria. The enriched feature set is incorporated into an MCIC framework based on the Hadi-Vencheh model. Experimental results show measurable reclassification effects when customer sentiment signals are included, demonstrating that integrating unstructured data into MCIC can enhance inventory prioritization.

logistics.title: Cross-Border Ownership and Input Access: Evidence from the Lithium Supply Chain
logistics.abstract: How does cross-border ownership shape the lithium supply chain? Using global data on mines and refineries, I estimate a model in which ownership can lower refiners' effective ore costs, encourage mines to restrict spot sales, and soften competition. To study these effects, I examine policies motivated by national security concerns about reliable access to critical mineral inputs: divestiture of Chinese stakes in overseas producers and a ban on ore exports to China. Divestiture increases spot ore supply but leaves lithium output nearly unchanged, while continued trade preserves Chinese access to ore. The export ban reduces global lithium supply because refining capacity elsewhere cannot fully replace lost Chinese production. Ownership transfers do not reserve ore for domestic production; restricting Chinese access imposes a substantial supply cost at existing capacities.

logistics.title: Distributionally Robust Dynamic Inventory Control: Automatic Recovery under Martingale Demand
logistics.authors: Jianzhi Leng, Daniel Zhuoyu Long, Lun Ran et al.
logistics.abstract: Problem definition: We study dynamic inventory control for battery-swapping stations that combine central replenishment with automatic local recovery. Central replenishment improves immediate battery availability but reduces the depleted-battery pool available for subsequent recovery, creating an intertemporal trade-off. Managing this trade-off is particularly challenging when historical demand data are limited and future demand is uncertain and temporally dependent. Methodology/results: We develop a time-consistent distributionally robust dynamic program under martingale demand ambiguity, using the latest observed demand as the next conditional mean without requiring a fully specified demand distribution. We establish an optimal order-up-to policy for every finite horizon and identify two critical recovery rates governing replenishment decisions. Under a regular penalty condition, we derive explicit finite-horizon policies and worst-case demand distributions, showing that sufficiently strong automatic recovery makes central replenishment unnecessary in nonterminal periods. Extensions to submartingale and supermartingale demand reveal contrasting behaviors, including eventual full-capacity replenishment under upward ambiguity and recovery-induced positive replenishment under downward ambiguity. logistics.title: Palimpsestic Accountability in the US Federal AI Inventories
logistics.authors: Dipto Das, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Aditya Vashistha et al.
logistics.abstract: An AI inventory is a structured, often public record in which a government or organization lists and describes the AI systems it uses or plans to use. Studies of single AI inventory releases describe what systems do but say little about how they are governed over time. We linked entries across three releases of the US Federal AI Use Case Inventory (2023--2025), compared answers only where both releases required them, and analyzed governance accounts through a dual deductive-inductive approach, guided by the Algorithmic Decision-Making Adapted for the Public Sector (ADMAPS) framework. As the inventory grew from 710 to 3,611 entries from 2023 to 2025, fewer required answers were left blank, but accountability was rewritten through three mechanisms. Each release \emph{redrew} the scope of the questions; agency-assigned classifications \emph{gated} what was reported; and answers were also \emph{overwritten}, with gains and losses concentrated in single agencies and little account of human oversight and judgment. These findings show that each release redraws the boundary of accountability and leaves the public to \emph{re-stitch} the records, a condition we term \textbf{palimpsestic accountability}. We recommend versioned records, reasons for every reclassification, public files that distinguish kinds of missing answers, and oversight documented as conditions to improve public…

logistics.title: Late Autumn: LLM Agents Specialize a General Multi-Robot Planner for One Warehouse
logistics.authors: Yimin Tang, Han Zhang, Shao-Hung Chan et al.
logistics.abstract: No algorithm is best on all problems, but a real warehouse is a narrow problem: its layout and processes rarely change. Operators still run one general multi-robot planner at many sites, because experts cannot tune it for each one. In this work, which we call Late Autumn, we explore whether LLM coding agents running autonomous research can specialize a general planner for one site, trading generality for throughput, much as post-training adapts a pretrained LLM to one task. We study six campaigns on a lifelong planner that combines task assignment with multi-agent path finding, on a floor modeled on an existing automated warehouse. We find that (1) the agents raise throughput by 22--60%, and the gains hold on unseen seeds; (2) they rediscover known MAPF mechanisms, such as corridor-exit priorities, local guidance, and rollouts, and independent campaigns find the same bottleneck; (3) the gains largely carry over to another layout, a larger fleet, and other service times, shrink with a smaller fleet, and mostly vanish under an outbound-heavy demand mix; and (4) each final patch (0.7k--2.4k lines) is a chain of scored commits with a median step of 27 lines, so experts can review it, and review finds problems that the score misses; some patches multiply planner compute by over 100x. logistics.title: Halal-NeSyNet: Clause-Scoped Neuro-Symbolic Cross-Attention for Automated Food Ingredient Auditing and Risk-Aware Halal Logistics Triage
logistics.authors: Mochamad Rizal Fauzan, Naila Nursyifa, Irgi Surya
logistics.abstract: Verifying that a packaged food is Halal requires reading ingredient declarations and E-number additives before goods enter certified warehouses. Dual-origin additives such as E471, E422, E441 and E920 are Mushbooh (doubtful) unless a botanical, microbial or certified-Halal qualifier appears in the same ingredient clause, so a plant-based qualifier on one clause must not clear an unqualified additive in another. We call a failure to respect this scope cross-clause modifier confounding and build a benchmark of 3,199 items (277 Open Food Facts records and 2,922 template-generated clause-swap items, labelled by an explicit 50-code rule base rather than by a certification authority) with a 540-item counterfactual suite. We propose Halal-NeSyNet, which couples a DistilBERT encoder with a 16-dimensional rule-derived symbolic vector through cross-attention and gated fusion, trained with an asymmetric false-Halal risk loss. Over five seeds, text-only TF-IDF baselines reach 86.25-86.71 % accuracy with 13.42-21.73 % false-Halal leakage and 6.33-26.00 % counterfactual triad consistency, whereas Halal-NeSyNet reaches 97.04+/-0.34 % and 99.67+/-0.50 %.
